findings.title: The opening explanation is written in needlessly technical language
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: I have to work out what it means, and I cannot make a proper judgement of the service from those words.

findings.title: Supporting text has weak contrast
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine…” and “Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK” are shown in pale grey or beige.
findings.why: I can see the large heading, but the smaller supporting text is difficult to read even at 200% zoom.

findings.title: Main image has no useful description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 577x440]
findings.why: I cannot tell whether it shows an example storybook or is only decoration.

findings.title: Primary action is vague
findings.evidence: [5] link "Proceed →"
findings.why: I am not told whether I will be taken to a form, a login, or the first creation step.

findings.title: Footer text is too faint and small to read
findings.evidence: Some text is too faint, including “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.”
findings.why: I cannot check the company details, privacy information, terms, or contact route.

findings.title: Login fields are not visibly labelled
findings.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email"; [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
findings.why: The pale placeholder writing may disappear or be hard to read at 200% zoom, and placeholders are not a dependable label.

findings.title: Footer links are too faint and small
findings.evidence: Privacy; Terms; Contact; and © 2026 StoryHearth Ltd. are marked faint/small text I cannot make out
findings.why: I cannot read the privacy, terms, or contact information, which makes the site feel less trustworthy.

findings.title: Error message gives no useful explanation or recovery
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I worry that I may have done something wrong, and I cannot tell whether the problem will affect my book.

findings.title: Profile sync failure is presented without reassurance
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I am left wondering whether the account is still safe to use or whether the book will be incomplete.

findings.title: Footer text is too faint to read
findings.evidence: The visible notes say “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are faint/small and cannot be read.
findings.why: I need to be able to check the privacy and contact information if I am unsure about the service.

findings.title: Important fields and Next button are below the fold
findings.evidence: The page says “everything below needs scrolling,” and [12] “Next” is offscreen.
findings.why: At 200% zoom I can only see a small part of the page, so I need to scroll carefully to discover the rest.

findings.title: Footer links are too faint to read
findings.evidence: [13], [14], and [15] are faint/small, and the footer text cannot be read.
findings.why: I cannot tell what those links say or where they will take me, so I would not use them.

findings.title: The Next button is below the visible area
findings.evidence: [19] button "Back" (offscreen); [20] button "Next" (offscreen)
findings.why: At 200% zoom, I cannot see what will move me to the next stage until I scroll.

findings.title: Example text is pale and low contrast
findings.evidence: Placeholder text such as "e.g. the beach at Grandma's" and "e.g. a yellow bucket" is very light grey.
findings.why: Pale writing is difficult for me to read with my macular degeneration, even when the browser is enlarged.

findings.title: Footer links are too small and faint to read
findings.evidence: The Privacy, Terms, and Contact links are described as faint or small, and the copyright text is unreadable.
findings.why: I cannot check the privacy, terms, or contact information because I cannot make out the words.

findings.title: Reading-level choices use unexplained jargon
findings.evidence: The heading is “Reading level”, followed only by “Lexile BR–200L”, “Lexile 200L–500L”, “Lexile 500L–800L”, and “Lexile 800L+”.
findings.why: I cannot confidently judge these labels for a four-year-old, so I may choose the wrong level and make the book too hard or too babyish.

findings.title: The preselected reading level is not explained
findings.evidence: “Lexile 200L–500L” is checked without any visible explanation of why that was selected.
findings.why: I can see the selection, but I do not know whether the site chose it because Lily is four or merely selected the middle option.

findings.title: Footer links are effectively invisible at this zoom
findings.evidence: The links labelled with faint, unreadable text lead to “/privacy.html”, “/privacy.html#terms”, and “mailto:hello@storyhearth.test”.
findings.why: I cannot find the privacy, terms, or contact information, which makes me less comfortable trusting the site with family memories.

findings.title: The story field silently cut off the end of my memory
findings.evidence: The action result says, “typed 300 characters … but the box now only shows 200 characters; the end of what you typed was cut off: ...'aginary gallop across the Norfolk fields. It matters because'”.
findings.why: The family memory itself is the heart of the book. If the site quietly loses words, I cannot trust what it will put into Lily's story.

findings.title: Photo upload control has no visible label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label); the screen only shows the native "Choose file" and "No file chosen" text
findings.why: I can see the heading and explanation, but a labelled control would make it easier to understand that I am choosing a file from this computer.

findings.title: Footer links are too faint to read
findings.evidence: [13], [14], and [15] are shown as faint/small text I cannot make out; the screen also shows faint copyright text
findings.why: Privacy, terms, and contact information matter when uploading family photos, but I cannot read these links at my current zoom.

findings.title: Spelling error in the generated title
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Lily”
findings.why: This is supposed to be a keepsake for Lily, and a misspelt title makes it look careless.

findings.title: The generated illustration style does not match my choice
findings.evidence: I selected “Storybook classic — timeless ink and colour,” but the page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic”.
findings.why: I wanted a traditional storybook appearance, and this looks like a different product from the one I selected.

findings.title: Page navigation uses tiny icon-only controls
findings.evidence: [6] button “‹” and [7] button “›”
findings.why: I use 200% zoom and struggle to hit small buttons; an arrow alone does not tell me exactly what it does.

findings.title: Important controls are shown below the fold
findings.evidence: [8] button “Regenerate entire book – $4.99” and [9] link “Order hardcover” are marked offscreen.
findings.why: I need to know what the book costs and what options exist before deciding whether to continue.

findings.title: The final sentence of the story is incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Lily looked up at the sky, she would always remember” followed immediately by “The End”
findings.why: It reads as a mistake rather than a proper ending, so I would not be happy giving this book to Lily as a keepsake.

findings.title: The page-turn buttons are too small for comfortable use
findings.evidence: [6] and [7] are shown as small arrow-only controls
findings.why: At 200% zoom I still struggle to hit such small targets, and the symbols alone do not clearly tell me which way I am turning.

findings.title: Gift wrap is pre-selected without being requested
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked); £7.99
findings.why: It quietly adds £7.99 to a £45.97 total before I have agreed to it, and I might miss a small box at 200% zoom.

findings.title: Countdown creates pressure at checkout
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57”
findings.why: I need time to inspect the delivery charge and unwanted extras, and this makes me worry about doing things too quickly.

findings.title: Shipping is a substantial charge that needs clearer context
findings.evidence: “Shipping & handling £12.99”
findings.why: That is more than half the hardcover price, and I need to know whether it applies to my address before judging the full cost.

findings.title: The misspelled book title is carried into the purchase
findings.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Lily”
findings.why: That title would be printed as it stands, and “Adventrue” looks careless and embarrassing in Lily’s book.

findings.title: Footer links are faint and too small to read
findings.evidence: [12], [13], [14] are marked “faint/small text you cannot make out”
findings.why: I cannot check the privacy, terms or contact information before entering personal and payment details.

findings.title: text_image_fit

findings.title: visual_quality

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text says Lily loves “Conker, the hand-carved wooden rocking horse,” but the picture contains no horse.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The stated appearance “strawberry-blonde bob, pink wellies” is not represented; Lily has a plain blond head, green top, dark trousers, and no visible pink wellies.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: “Once upon a time” and “there lived a curious child” make the opening sound more formal than the requested reading age of four.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: “The ephemeral luminescence of the crepuscular firmament engendered an inexplicable melancholy, juxtaposing ineffable wonder with existential trepidation” contains advanced, abstract vocabulary and is far above reading age four.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The story abruptly changes from Lily loving Conker to unexplained melancholy without saying what caused it.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: Lily faces forward rather than looking upward, and the picture does not show any sadness or melancholy.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The child's name is misspelled as “Lil” in “as Lil pulled up her hood.”

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text describes pouring rain, puddles, a hood, and Lily holding Conker, while the image shows a dry sunny field and a stationary child.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The sudden rain is not shown, and there is no cause for Lily to run away from the shed into a threatening adventure.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: “Uncle Bartholomew” is invented; the only requested family character was “Grandpa Harold.”

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: “Lily, follow me!” is followed by “and he followed him,” reversing the expected action and leaving the referents confused.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Grandpa Harold is replaced by an invented uncle and never appears as a character.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The picture does not show Lily following the uncle along a winding path, and it omits Conker despite this being a continuing journey.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: “The shadows grew teeth and whispered that no one would ever find Lily again” introduces threatening imagery and abandonment anxiety for a four-year-old.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The shiny red balloon and dark-woods peril were invented and are not connected to the family memory.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text calls for deep woods, teeth-like shadows, trembling, and darkness, but Lily smiles in an open clearing beside an unexplained balloon.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: Lily is moved into deep woods and given a balloon without any transition or explanation.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “Once upon a time, in Harold's workshop shed and the Norfolk fields, there lived a curious child named Lily” duplicates the opening sentence from page 3.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The page jumps from being lost or frightened in the woods to walking home without explaining how Lily became safe or where home is.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The story says Lily “skipped all the way home,” while the image shows her standing still in the same generic field with no Conker.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The requested Christmas gift and the family-keepsake message are still absent.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “She would always remember” ends without saying what she remembered and without final punctuation.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “The End” is printed both before and after the unfinished closing sentence.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The closing thought omits Conker, Christmas, Grandpa Harold's carving, and the keepsake passed down with love.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The unfinished sky memory has not been prepared as a meaningful conclusion and does not resolve the invented danger.

findings.title: emotional_resonance
findings.evidence: The final personal message about a handmade family keepsake is absent.
